old_problem: This exact source row names Processors in Items and its same-row DeepSeek resource, but directs the operator to Fans in Procedure. The generic SPEC criterion does not select a resource, member list, field matrix, topology/location relation or absent-state behavior. Processor and fan resources are different inventory populations; the adjacent DIMM row is a separately preserved source conflict and cannot define this one.
disposition_reason: Retain Engineering Decision Pending, source conflict and a REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION classification. This is not irreducibly BLOCKED: each branch has a safe, read-only, parameterizable collection/UI method once the owner selects it and supplies its corresponding SPEC/schema. It cannot be RESOLVED today because choosing Processors from title/DeepSeek or Fans from Procedure would silently discard the other literal source scope. The new overlay therefore preserves two mutually exclusive execution branches, prohibits verdict-bearing collection until the owner selects Processors, Fans or separately accepted checkpoints, and defines the complete evidence/safety contract for the selected branch.
decision_basis: The exact XLSX Functionality row 1622, matching same-row DeepSeek/test-json fields, exact V2 and V3.1 historical reviews, source-conflict/Engineering-Decision records, code/variant history and the locked queue were read directly. The next formal identity was directly opened as row 1623 / Wistron-BMC-00894-V002 / 58d1159b7fecbdfd from the reconstructed immutable queue and XLSX; it was not inferred from test-code sequencing.

Items and the DeepSeek resource name Processors; Procedure literally says Fans. Processor and fan collections differ in member identity, topology/location, fields, health semantics and expected SPEC rows, so one response cannot prove the other branch.

The `all information` criterion has no processor socket/member/topology or fan member/location/status matrix. The DeepSeek Name/ProcessorType/Model projection is insufficient even if Processors is later selected and its TLS/credential form must not be reused.

Both candidate activities are non-mutating BMC inventory observations. A scoped BMC-Web/API/Redfish collection, protected credentials/TLS, complete member retrieval and UI capture can be parameterized safely after an owner scope decision; no policy write, sensor/configuration change, log clear, power action or physical operation is needed.

The required BMC-Web UI/photos are evidence-bearing. Redfish or another read-only interface can corroborate the chosen collection but cannot replace the required UI observation; inventory evidence must remain same-SUT, complete and time-correlated.

No ED-12 source-key-approved copied-word correction exists for this row. ED-24 therefore requires preserving its conflict in an overlay rather than treating Processors as automatically authoritative; ED-02/ED-21 preserve this distinct Source Key and prevent adjacent DIMM/fan cases from supplying its answer.

ED-03/ED-13 permit a documented standard BMC read draft but prohibit guessed OEM/UI semantics; ED-20 requires true WebUI evidence; ED-26 bars automatic repeat; ED-33/ED-35/ED-36/ED-38 retain Master/coverage, distinguish readiness from execution and prohibit a DUT verdict.

test_case.test_name: Inventory and LEDs - Processors — parameterized scope-decision contract
test_case.purpose: Preserve both literal row-1622 inventory scopes until the owner selects the authoritative one: either validate the complete Processor inventory, validate the complete Fan inventory, or approve two separately reported checkpoints. The review does not merge, substitute or execute either branch before that decision.
required_package: Owner disposition selecting Processors, Fans or separately accepted checkpoints while preserving the Master conflict; selected collection/UI target and explicit treatment of the unselected branch
Exact same-SUT/BMC and BMC firmware/UI identity, protected BMC-Web/API access with validated TLS, secure credential handling and non-cached evidence storage

If Processors is selected: complete expected socket/member/topology/availability and field matrix (for example identity/vendor/model/type/core/thread/part/serial where supported), resource schema and absent/disabled/virtual/stale rules
If Fans is selected: complete expected member/location/physical association/status/speed/health and field matrix, resource schema and absent/redundant/stale rules

Source-required BMC-Web screenshots/photos, complete collection plus every member payload/page, approved independent BIOS/OS/topology correlation where applicable, no-mutation audit and engineer-owned eventual verdict
test_case.test_command: NOT STARTED — parameterized read-only contract. Do not issue a verdict-bearing Processor or Fan query until the owner selects the source branch. After selection, capture same-target BMC-Web Inventory and LEDs screenshots/photos plus the complete approved collection and every member resource using a protected documented interface; normalize all approved members/fields, compare with that branch's signed SPEC/schema matrix, identify missing/extra/duplicate/stale/malformed/mismatched entries, correlate approved topology/location evidence, preserve relevant logs without clearing them and report the evidence for engineer disposition. Do not use `curl -k`, password-on-command-line credentials, a three-field projection, cached/cross-host data, a guessed OEM URI or an API-only substitute for required UI evidence.
test_case.expected_result: Before the owner ruling, the expected result is only the selected authoritative inventory scope and its complete expected member/field matrix. After a Processors selection, every in-scope processor member and approved field must compare to the Processor matrix; after a Fans selection, every in-scope fan member and approved field must compare to the Fan matrix. If two checkpoints are approved, each must produce distinct scope-labelled evidence and verdict inputs. No current DUT PASS/FAIL is claimed.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: Retain Engineering Decision Pending while scope, matching matrix or disposition of the literal opposing source branch is unknown. Once selected, PASS requires complete same-SUT BMC-Web and collection/member evidence, one-to-one member identity/topology-or-location comparison and no unexplained expected/actual difference under the approved matrix; missing, extra, duplicate, stale, malformed or mismatched data is reported as an exception for the engineer. A partial three-field query, collection count alone, neighboring DIMM/Fan data, generic SPEC assertion or successful HTTP response is not a PASS basis. Final DUT PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED remains engineer-owned.
safety_gate: Do not silently call Fans a typo, select Processors from the DeepSeek URI, or combine processor and fan evidence under one generic result.
Keep this inventory inspection read-only: do not change processor/fan/thermal/power/BIOS/BMC controls, workload state or hardware population.
Do not clear SEL, dmesg, syslog, audit trails or existing inventory evidence for a baseline; review relevant deltas without destructive cleanup.
Verify same-SUT BMC/host/UI identity and complete member scope before comparison; reject cached, cross-host, stale or partial payloads as evidence.
Use protected credentials and validated TLS; do not disable certificate verification or expose secrets in command lines, output, screenshots or commits.
Do not replace source-required BMC-Web visual evidence/photos with an API readback; automation can assist collection and comparison after the approved scope is known.
No automatic retry or DUT verdict is authorized; stop interpretation on unresolved scope or incomplete evidence and preserve the raw capture.
expected_evidence: Exact Source Key/variant, row hash, literal Processors/Fans conflict, same-row DeepSeek/V2/history and owner scope ruling
Redacted same-SUT/BMC/UI identity, firmware/UI version, signed selected-scope matrix/schema and timestamped source-required BMC-Web screenshots/photos
Complete selected collection and all member payloads/pages; normalized membership/field comparison; approved Processor topology or Fan location correlation; exception analysis
Relevant BMC/SEL/audit review without log clearing, protected-session/no-mutation audit and evidence provenance
Current no-command/no-scope-selection/no-DUT-verdict record, and eventual engineer-owned PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED decision after the selected branch is executed
test_case.recovery: The Review-layer plan authorizes no mutation, so recovery is limited to stopping interpretation, retaining the raw collection/member/UI captures, closing the protected BMC session and confirming that processor, fan, BIOS, power and BMC configuration remained unchanged. Do not alter inventory, clear logs, reboot or retry to manufacture a result. If a project later uses an unexpected write, it requires a new approved mutation/recovery contract and fresh review.

source_conflict.reason: Items/DeepSeek designate Processors, while the literal Procedure designates Fans. The overlay preserves both competing inventories and does not choose one from likelihood.

blocked.reason: The operation is safely understood as read-only inventory capture after an owner scope/matrix decision. Scope selection and SPEC/schema are unresolved project/engineering inputs, not an unsafe unknown write, destructive stimulus or irrecoverable operation; execution readiness remains withheld until supplied.

pending.remaining_project_configuration: Owner selection of Processors, Fans or separate checkpoints; disposition of unselected literal source branch; selected complete member/field/SPEC/schema matrix; same-SUT BMC/UI/API mapping; topology/location and special-state rules; protected access/evidence and engineer-verdict workflow.
pending.execution_status: NOT STARTED; NO BMC/WEBUI/API INVENTORY COLLECTION USED AS VERDICT EVIDENCE, NO CONFIGURATION/LOG/POWER/BIOS/CPU/FAN/DUT ACTION AUTHORIZED OR EXECUTED BEFORE SCOPE RULING

project_authority: The BMC/platform owner selects the inventory scope and signs its field/membership matrix; the test owner supplies SPEC/schema and exception rules; the operator captures required BMC-Web evidence; the engineer owns the final verdict. They may resolve the current run only in an overlay, not edit Master, reuse adjacent DIMM data, turn a Processors API projection into Fan evidence or waive required visual evidence.
